papers.title: Heat shock-induced autophagy has cargo selectivity in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
papers.summary: In yeast, heat shock triggers autophagy that selectively degrades ubiquitinated protein aggregates via the macroaggrephagy receptor Cue5. Heat stress also drives turnover of the aggrephagy receptor CCT2 and polyQ-huntingtin, though vacuole-dependently yet independent of canonical autophagy. Autophagy is cytoprotective for recovery after heat stress, with possible implications for heat-based therapeutics.

papers.title: G3BP1 depletion, observed in Parkinson's Disease, drives Golgi-lysosome-autophagy defects.
papers.summary: G3BP1, depleted in several neurodegenerative diseases, stabilizes the COPI vesicle protein β-COP via USP10. Depletion disrupts this, accelerating β-COP proteasomal degradation, impairing Golgi structure, lysosomal homeostasis and autophagic flux, and slowing α-synuclein clearance. Both G3BP1 and β-COP are reduced in Parkinson's disease/dementia with Lewy bodies brains and a PD mouse model, linking vesicular trafficking to proteostasis.

papers.title: Ninjurin-1 mediates hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury.
papers.summary: Membrane protein Ninjurin-1 (NINJ1) aggregates to permeabilize cells during lytic death pathways driving hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI). NINJ1 is elevated in human liver and correlates with early allograft dysfunction. Genetic deletion or pharmacologic inhibition reduced injury in mouse/rat segmental IRI models; hepatocyte and Kupffer cell NINJ1 both contribute. NINJ1 is a candidate therapeutic target for liver transplantation.

papers.title: IDE-mediated GLP-1 degradation as the basis for designing long-acting and CNS-stable GLP-1 receptor agonists.
papers.summary: Insulin-degrading enzyme (IDE) is identified as a previously unknown GLP-1-degrading protease with two cleavage sites, regulating glucose control independently of insulin. D-amino acid substitutions in GLP-1 and semaglutide confer stability in plasma, liver, and CNS. D-Ser18-semaglutide shows prolonged plasma retention and sustained glucose lowering. This informs long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonists for metabolic and CNS use.

papers.title: Metabolic control of smooth muscle cell phenotype switching in atherosclerosis.
papers.summary: Metabolic control of smooth muscle cell (SMC) contractile phenotype in atherosclerosis is examined. TGFβ suppresses PDK4, enabling ACSS2-dependent acetyl-CoA production that stabilizes R-Smads and preserves SMC contractility. SMC-specific PDK4 knockout reduced atherosclerosis in ApoE-/- mice, and PDK4 levels correlate with human atherosclerosis severity. PDK4 and carbohydrate metabolism regulate SMC contractile state via TGFβ signaling.

papers.title: Muscular dystrophy-associated lamin variants disrupt cellular organization through a nucleolar-ribosomal axis.
papers.summary: Using C. elegans models of Emery-Dreifuss muscular dystrophy, lamin variants are shown to reduce cytoplasmic mesoscale crowding, increase diffusivity, and disrupt nuclear positioning and ER architecture—phenotypes of ribosome depletion. Lamin dysfunction lowers nucleolar fibrillarin and ribosome abundance via a nucleolar-ribosomal axis. LEM-domain protein loss phenocopies lamin mutants, linking nuclear architecture to whole-cell biophysics and suggesting ribosome-restoring therapies.

papers.title: Insulin-like growth factor-binding protein 7 is a soluble cell adhesion molecule.
papers.summary: Cryo-EM reveals IGFBP7 assembles into a barrel-shaped dodecamer in heparin presence. The C-terminal IgC2 domain forms the barrel core, capped by N-terminal heparin-binding IB domains. This homo-oligomer engages heparan sulfate proteoglycans on adjacent cells, acting as soluble 'cell glue' for cell-cell adhesion and prolonging RTK (insulin receptor, c-Met) signaling. IG FBP7 is a universal adhesion factor explaining its pleiotropy.

papers.title: The molecular basis of mitochondrial crista formation by the MIC10 complex.
papers.summary: Multiscale simulations and structure prediction reveal the MIC10 subcomplex (Mic10, Mic26, Mic27) of MICOS strongly recruits cardiolipin at conserved positive loop motifs, driving subunit oligomerization and stabilizing membrane curvature. Reconstruction of the full MIC10 complex maintains cristae bending, while disordered regions may form a permeability barrier between cristae and intermembrane space. This provides a mechanistic model of cristae curvature formation.

papers.title: An axon-intrinsic loop restricts nerve regeneration through axonal protein synthesis.
papers.summary: Injured axons synthesize KH domain RNA-binding protein KHSRP, which promotes mRNA decay and slows regeneration. Elevated axonal Ca2+ activates KHSRP translation; alternating Reg3a and KHSRP translation sustains KHSRP. Reg3a stimulates ER Ca2+ release, activating PERK, eIF2α phosphorylation, and KHSRP translation, accelerating regeneration when depleted in vivo. This is a localized translation signaling loop that decelerates axon growth.

papers.title: Bacteriophage PAK_P3 genome structuration and dynamics during infection of Pseudomonas aeruginosa reveal specific interaction patterns.
papers.summary: The spatial genome dynamics of virulent dsDNA phage PAK_P3 during Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection were mapped. The phage genome rapidly decondenses to adopt a specific 3D organization reflecting its transcriptional program, while the host genome decondenses as expression wanes. Specific phage-host genome contacts reveal how the phage exploits host spatial genome architecture during infection, highlighting genome folding in viral infection.

papers.title: Activation of G(12)-type G proteins in pancreatic β cells protects against impaired glucose homeostasis.
papers.summary: G12-type G protein signaling in pancreatic β cells was explored using gene knockout and β-cell-specific chemogenetics. Selective activation of β-cell G12 signaling strongly promoted insulin secretion, protecting against obesity-associated metabolic deficits and improving glycemic control in a T2D mouse model. ROCK was identified as a key downstream effector. G12-linked GPCRs may be targets for antidiabetic drugs.

papers.title: Carbon ion irradiation at a clinically used dose rewires super-enhancers to drive necroptosis and systemic immunity.
papers.summary: A physical dose of 2 Gy carbon ions (high-LET) provokes antitumor immunity independent of dose. Carbon ions redirect death to MLKL-dependent necroptosis and trigger an NF-κB inflammatory cascade, surpassing 8 Gy X-rays in immunogenicity. Multi-omics link DNA-damage-driven super-enhancer remodeling that suppresses apoptosis while licensing necroptosis. In vivo, 2 Gy carbon ion treatment drives abscopal responses, supporting radio-immunotherapy integration.

papers.title: Cardiac tertiary immune niches drive immune activation in immune checkpoint inhibitor myocarditis.
papers.summary: In a pharmacological mouse model of immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) myocarditis, spatial and single-cell analyses identified Ly6C+ monocyte and PD-1+ CD8+ T cell infiltration organizing into fibroblast-rich 'tertiary T cell niches' (TTCNs) that serve as hubs of T cell activation. A TTCN signature was enriched in patient hearts. TTCN-associated cytokines are candidate targets to reduce ICI cardiotoxicity.

papers.title: Algae-specific immune modulation influences responses to heat and pathogen challenge in a symbiotic coral.
papers.summary: Algal symbiont type influences coral immunity in Pocillopora acuta. Durusdinium-hosting corals show higher immune gene expression and NF-κB levels but suffer tissue loss and immune dysregulation under heat, whereas Cladocopium-hosted corals bleach and lose nitrogen-fixing bacteria. Vibrio infection caused high tissue loss only in Durusdinium-hosting corals. Durusdinium confers thermotolerance yet predisposes corals to tissue damage under multiple stressors.

papers.title: Loss of the mitochondrial SAM transporter reveals a lipoylation-dependent metabolic vulnerability in the postnatal heart.
papers.summary: Mitochondrial S-adenosylmethionine (mitoSAM) import via SLC25A26 becomes limiting after birth specifically restricting protein lipoylation. Loss of SLC25A26 impaired lipoylation-dependent flux through pyruvate and α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenases, depleting aspartate and nucleotides, linked to sustained cardiomyocyte cycling, delayed maturation, and early cardiomyopathy. Medium-chain triglyceride supplementation partially stabilized metabolism. Lipoylation is the most mitoSAM-sensitive pathway during postnatal heart adaptation.

papers.title: Truthful visualizations for mass spectrometry imaging enable high-spatial-resolution interactive m/z mapping and exploration.
papers.summary: MSI-Visual is an open-source framework for mass spectrometry imaging that integrates truthful dimensionality-reduction visualizations with region-of-interest selection, statistical comparison, and direct m/z mapping. It introduces four visualization strategies (SALo, SPEAR, ToP3, PR3D) for global structure preservation and memory-efficient visualization. Benchmarks and lipidomics cases (mouse brain, kidney pathology) show improved detection of subtle tissue differences, supporting discovery and diagnostic MSI workflows.

papers.title: Multiheme selenoenzyme essential for elemental sulfur respiration.
papers.summary: A conserved multiheme cytochrome c selenoprotein essential for elemental sulfur respiration is identified in a sulfur-respiring bacterium. The enzyme forms a tetramer, each subunit with five hemes and one selenocysteine. It catalyzes polysulfide reduction at an active site where cysteine coordinates heme iron and selenocysteine is essential for catalysis; both residues are critical in vivo. This reveals selenium-sulfur-dependent catalysis on a heme center.

papers.title: RIBOTAC-mediated degradation of hsa-microRNA-301a-3p suppresses TNBC bone metastasis.
papers.summary: Through integrative bioinformatics and machine learning, hsa-microRNA-301a-3p was identified as a central regulator of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) bone metastasis. A ribonuclease-targeting chimera (RIBOTAC) that recruits RNase L was designed to degrade pri-miR-301a, restoring NEDD4L expression and promoting YAP degradation, suppressing TNBC bone metastasis. RNA-targeted degradation is demonstrated as a therapeutic strategy.

papers.title: Message in a Bottle: The Therapeutic Potential of Domesticated Capsid Proteins.
papers.summary: This Annual Review examines domesticated Gag capsid (CA) proteins derived from LTR retrotransposons, widely present in mammals and other metazoans. Many retain the ability to assemble capsid-like particles packaging RNA and other biomolecules, with roles in intercellular communication and gene regulation. Recent work exploits these for delivery applications. Domesticated Gag CA proteins may offer lower immunogenicity, flexible cargo capacity, and tissue-specific targeting versus AAVs, LNPs, and lentiviral systems.

papers.title: Surface and global proteomics identify ROR2 and other proteins as potentially actionable immunotherapeutic targets in osteosarcoma.
papers.summary: Surface and global proteomics of 22 osteosarcoma (OS) patient-derived xenografts identified surface proteins for immunotherapy, including known candidates (LRRC15, MMP14, MRC2, CADM1) and poorly characterized targets ROR2 and TMEM119. Both ROR2 and TMEM119 are robustly expressed in OS but limited/none in normal pediatric tissues, and their loss reduces OS cell migration. This provides a resource of potentially actionable OS targets.

papers.title: LAMTOR1 sorts APP to late endosomes via AP-3-mediated trafficking.
papers.summary: LAMTOR1 is identified as a novel APP intracellular domain binding partner that sorts APP from early to late endosomes. LAMTOR1 knockout reduced APP trafficking to late endosomes, promoting amyloidogenic processing on early endosomes and increasing Aβ; neuronal conditional knockout impaired memory in an AD mouse model. Sorting is mediated by AP-3 binding LAMTOR1. LAMTOR1 is a potential AD therapeutic target.

papers.title: Contribution of mechanical forces in multiciliated cell differentiation.
papers.summary: This review examines how mechanical forces regulate multiciliated cell differentiation. Multiciliated cells move fluids in brain, airways, and reproductive organs; dysfunction causes airway infections, subfertility, and ventricular enlargement. Drawing on airway, brain ventricle, and Xenopus systems, the authors propose mechanical cues act as contextual regulators that enable, time, and control the multiciliated differentiation program interacting with transcription factors and cell-cycle regulators.

papers.title: Challenges and opportunities in type III secretion system effector prediction.
papers.summary: This review covers the conceptual evolution of type III secretion system effector (T3SE) prediction, from empirical N-terminal features and feature-engineered ML to deep learning and pipelines integrating homology, regulatory elements, and genome context. Persistent challenges include biased training data toward well-known pathogens and unclear generalization to symbiotic/environmental bacteria. The authors call for centralized, user-friendly platforms producing transparent, ranked outputs for validation.

papers.title: Tailless (TLX) terminates the neural stem cell temporal cascade in both the optic lobe and central brain.
papers.summary: Tailless (TLX), a terminal temporal factor in optic lobe neural stem cells, also acts as a terminal factor in intermediate neural progenitors (INPs), demonstrating functional conservation. TLX is activated by the preceding factor Scarecrow, represses odd-paired and hamlet, and partially promotes gliogenesis. Targeted DamID genome-wide binding in both cell types reveals conserved and divergent targets, showing conserved temporal patterning with lineage-specific outputs.

papers.title: Early glucagon-positive cells restrict pancreatic branching through VMAT2-noradrenaline-mediated ROS signaling.
papers.summary: In pancreatic bud explant cultures, inhibiting VMAT2-mediated catecholamine uptake promotes epithelial branching and increases insulin-expressing cells, mimicked by inhibiting tyrosine hydroxylase, MAO-A, dopamine β-hydroxylase, or norepinephrine transporter. ROS play a role in branch formation. Early Gcg- and Ins-co-expressing cells express VMAT2; lineage-specific deletion increases branching and islet area while decreasing ROS. These cells regulate pancreatic branching via VMAT2-noradrenaline-ROS signaling.

papers.title: Attachment performance of cuttlefish (Sepia officinalis) suckers depends on the interaction between papillae and substrate topography.
papers.journal: Journal of the Royal Society, Interface
papers.summary: Cuttlefish (Sepia officinalis) sucker attachment was tested ex vivo on substrates varying in stiffness and roughness. Attachment forces varied significantly with roughness, peaking where roughness coincided with average papillae height (RMS ~6.84 µm), and were higher on stiffer substrates. A mathematical model for leakage across the sucker rim qualitatively agrees. Papillae aid attachment to natural prey and could inform bioinspired suction cup design.

papers.title: Dynamic micropatterning uncovers spatial dynamics of B cell immune synapse formation.
papers.summary: A dynamic micropatterning technique models B cell immunological synapse (IS) formation with spatial and temporal control, enabling imaging before/after BCR engagement. In A20 D1.3 mouse B cells, distinct spatial distributions of BCR-proximal signaling proteins were found, and initial adhesion size/shape modulated signaling. Enhanced-resolution 3D microscopy revealed cells repurposing pre-existing actin protrusions as building blocks for the IS, providing insight into early IS formation.

papers.title: A 3D printable device for non-invasive longitudinal neuroimaging in the adult zebrafish.
papers.summary: A 3D-printable device enables non-invasive, repeatable multiphoton neural imaging of genetically non-pigmented adult zebrafish across ages and sizes. Animals recovered after multi-hour sessions and were imaged repeatedly over weeks to years. Utility was shown imaging dynamic neuroimmune cells, radial glia, and oligodendrocytes. This supports longitudinal studies of aging and neurodegeneration and other cell-scale neuroimaging in adult fish.

papers.title: Comparative genomics reveals signatures of distinct metabolic strategies and gene loss associated with Hydra immortality.
papers.summary: A chromosome-level genome assembly of Hydra vulgaris (strain AEP.Jnig) is reported. Gene-body hypermethylation correlates with transcriptional stability. The immortal H. vulgaris paradoxically lacks canonical anti-aging genes (e.g., klotho, NAMPT) present in aging-inducible H. oligactis, instead showing a distinct metabolic signature of mitochondrial energy production and NTP biosynthesis. These results suggest mechanisms underlying Hydra immortality and aging traits, providing targets for functional studies.

papers.title: Apical actin filament turnover mediated by cyclase-associated protein coordinates non-centrosomal microtubules in epithelium.
papers.summary: In the Drosophila follicular epithelium, loss of cyclase-associated protein (Cap), a regulator of actin turnover, causes apical actin accumulation. The CapRD domain is the principal activity preventing this. Excess apical actin depletes apical microtubules and mislocalizes the crosslinker Shot; acute disruption partially restores both. Cap-dependent actin turnover spatially regulates non-centrosomal microtubule organization and epithelial architecture in vivo.

papers.title: Cystinosin/Ers1 functions in redox homeostasis in the early secretory pathway.
papers.summary: Ers1, the yeast homolog of cystinosin, localizes to and functions in the early secretory pathway and does not transport cystine. Ers1 genetically interacts with early-secretory recycling adaptors and redox-active Fe-S cluster-binding proteins. Cystinosin-LKG, an alternately spliced isoform with altered localization, can functionally replace Ers1 in yeast. This uncovers a conserved cystinosin/Ers1 role in early secretory pathway redox homeostasis, informing cystinosis pathology.

papers.title: Engineering peptides into antibodies-opportunities and strategies for therapeutic innovation.
papers.summary: This review examines strategies merging peptides and antibodies for therapeutics: peptide grafting into hypervariable/framework loops, terminal fusion to antibody chains, Fc-peptide fusions, and bioconjugation. Insertion site, peptide topology, and linker design affect folding, activity, and developability. Fusions can confer new target binding, conditional activation, altered biodistribution, or intracellular delivery. Challenges include manufacturability, stability, heterogeneity, and immunogenicity, with protein design and bioconjugation advancing the field.

papers.title: Emerging experimental and computational methods for studying redox-regulated structural transitions.
papers.summary: This review covers emerging experimental and computational methods for studying redox-regulated structural transitions. Chemoselective probes enable high-purity trapping of sulfenic/sulfinic states, while machine learning, graph neural networks, and protein language models enable proteome-wide redox-switch prediction. Redox modifications drive conditional folding transitions in intrinsically disordered proteins and condensates. Integration of generative diffusion models could enable real-time simulation of multi-state structural ensembles across the redox proteome.

papers.title: Proteomic analysis reveals a metabolic switch and cellular remodeling in pancreatic-like cell spheroids cocultured with hepatocyte-like cells using an interconnected liver-pancreas-on-chip system.
papers.summary: An organ-on-chip device hosting hiPSC-derived liver and pancreatic tissues was used to study liver-pancreas crosstalk by proteomics. Co-culture with liver enhanced pancreatic ECM remodeling, inflammatory, and pro-apoptotic proteins, while Pan monocultures had higher fatty acid metabolism, glycolysis, and TCA proteins and upregulated pancreatic markers (GCG, TPH1, SCGN3, SCGN, CHGA, CHGB). Results reveal a metabolic switch with cellular stress, guiding multicellular organ-on-chip design.

papers.title: Revisiting differential expression analysis: An updated six-dimensional comparative study.
papers.summary: This study compared 12 differential expression methods across 80 simulated and real datasets, in a six-dimensional evaluation (accuracy, low-FDR sensitivity, false positives, stability, outlier robustness, noise robustness). No single method dominated; at n=3 ABSSeq generally performed best, and at n=5 DESeq2 and edgeR v4 gained sensitivity. Wilcoxon and ROTS were noise-robust. A 'Bagua' map and decision tree guide method selection, balancing accuracy and consistency.

papers.title: Linguistic markers of deception in Arabic news headlines: A cross-corpus study of stylistic and numeric features.
papers.summary: This study investigated automatic fake-news detection in Arabic headlines using five heterogeneous corpora and a unified combination, with English sets incorporated via neural machine translation. Linguistic analysis revealed stable veracity asymmetries. Transformers outperformed classical baselines; late fusion coupling transformers with engineered features improved results only on datasets with numeric/temporal cues. Even where accuracy gains were marginal, interpretable features enhanced explainability for Arabic misinformation detection.

papers.title: Bovine serum albumin sensitizes the mouse brain to lipopolysaccharides.
papers.summary: The role of bovine serum albumin (BSA) in LPS-induced brain injury was examined in mice. At 5 mg/kg, BSA-LPS enhanced brain autofluorescence, vascular-cell permeability (PI co-localization with CD31/CD13), HRP leakage, and pyroptosis markers (gasdermin D, CD11b, CD68) versus LPS alone; differences disappeared at 25 mg/kg. Albumin bound LPS in brain, increasing its entry into brain parenchyma. Albumin likely boosts LPS brain effects by binding it.

papers.title: Systems pharmacology reveals type I interferon and myeloid-like B cell reprogramming as candidate druggable axes in antiphospholipid syndrome.
papers.summary: An integrative systems pharmacology approach (WGCNA, single-cell RNA-seq, CMAP, docking) prioritized targets in antiphospholipid syndrome, identifying two disease modules (ME10, IFN-I signaling; ME2, degranulation/innate activation). Single-cell analysis revealed transitional B cells with aberrant SPI1 and myeloid-like reprogramming. CMAP ranked chloroquine among top ME2 candidates. A 3-gene signature (CORO1A, ANKRD22, IFITM1) achieved AUC 0.802. This framework generates hypotheses for pathway-guided APS therapy requiring validation.

papers.title: Multifaceted response of microglia in the cuprizone model of demyelination.
papers.summary: Microglial dynamics were characterized in the cuprizone demyelination model. Microglial number and area increased dramatically by 1 week and persisted through 4 weeks, with partial recovery during remyelination. Early demyelination showed microglial morphological remodeling, myelin engulfment, increased Mertk and ApoE, and decreased TNF and IFNb1. In the retina (no myelin), microglia lacked morphological changes but downregulated CD68, indicating cuprizone exerts direct effects on microglia beyond demyelination.

papers.title: Protonophore uncouplers and the decoupler α,ω-hexadecanedioic acid relieve the succinate-induced blockade of glutamate and malate oxidation in the resting state (state 4).
papers.summary: In state-4 liver mitochondria, succinate oxidation suppresses glutamate and malate oxidation (half-maximal at ~220 µM succinate) via reverse electron transport at complex I. Protonophore uncouplers (FCCP, palmitic acid, chenodeoxycholic acid) and the decoupler α,ω-hexadecanedioic acid alleviate this suppression when respiration is stimulated no more than ~2-fold. Under RET, uncouplers and decoupler similarly inhibit H2O2 generation; the decoupler's effects may involve switching complex III to idle mode.

papers.title: Metabolomic and transcriptomic analyses reveal the monoterpenoid indole alkaloid biosynthesis in Neolamarckia cadamba.
papers.summary: Untargeted metabolomics (GC-MS) and RNA-seq of leaves, bark, and fruit of Neolamarckia cadamba identified 281 metabolites; fruit showed highest diversity with 74 tissue-specific metabolites (flavonoids, shikimic, quinic acids), while bark/leaves were terpenoid/amino-acid enriched. Transcriptomics identified monoterpenoid indole alkaloid biosynthesis genes including secologanin synthase, strictosidine synthase, tryptophan decarboxylase, and loganic acid O-methyltransferase (validated by RT-qPCR). This foundation supports metabolic engineering and functional genomics.

papers.title: Dual knockdown of Scn1b and Gsdmd induces an M2-like functional state in macrophages and modulates inflammation and fibrosis in a rat model of acute respiratory distress syndrome.
papers.summary: Dual knockdown of Scn1b and Gsdmd (differentially expressed in M2 macrophages) induced an M2-like state, shifting metabolism toward oxidative phosphorylation without affecting phagocytosis. Conditioned medium enhanced MSC proliferation. In an LPS ARDS rat model, M(Scn1b+Gsdmd) macrophages reduced IL-18 and TIMP2 after 24h and promoted reparative signatures at 7 days (increased VEGF, reduced septal thickening and collagen). Dual knockdown supports macrophage-based ARDS cell therapy.

papers.title: Subcellular localization of human long non-coding RNAs is an isoform-resolved property masked by gene-level analysis.
papers.summary: Subcellular localization of human long non-coding RNAs was assessed as an isoform-resolved property using ENCODE fractionation RNA-seq across 15 cell lines (1,262 isoforms). Gene-level analysis masks within-gene heterogeneity: reproducible compartment calls show 21.4% of genes masked (vs 3.1% expected) or 14.8% under the strictest criterion. Results reproduced across labs and quantifiers. Tissue switching doesn't preferentially cross compartments, and differences aren't explained by Alu content, 3'-end usage, structure, or translation.

papers.title: The Reductive Stress Nexus: Integrated Pathways of Metabolic Dysregulation, Senescence and Blood-Brain Barrier Failure in Neurodegenerative Disease and Brain Aging.
papers.summary: This review examines reductive stress—a pathological shift toward hyper-reduced redox couples—within the neurovascular unit maintaining blood-brain barrier integrity. Chronic antioxidant activation expanding the reduced thiol pool suppresses ROS signaling, impairs mitochondria, induces ER stress/UPR, dysregulates calcium, promotes DNA damage, senescence, and inflammasome activation. Reductive stress forms an integrated network with oxidative, nitrosative, and glycation stresses. Reliable identification requires simultaneous, compartment-resolved redox measurement.

papers.title: Berberine Modulates Mitophagy-Related Gene Expression and Suppresses Breast Cancer Cells: A Multi-Omics and Experimental Study.
papers.summary: Berberine's anti-breast cancer effects through mitophagy were investigated via GEO data, single-cell sequencing, molecular docking, and in vitro experiments. Twenty pivotal autophagy-related genes were identified; autophagy and mitophagy pathways were markedly activated in breast cancer. Single-cell analysis linked macrophage-invasion-mediated fibroblast and NK cell changes to the mechanism. Berberine inhibited breast cancer by targeting BECN1, BCL2, HIF1A, MYC, PINK1, and FOXO3 to regulate autophagy and mitochondrial quality control.

papers.title: Mitochondrial genome and phylogenetic analysis of Aster Indicus L.
papers.summary: The mitochondrial genome of Aster indicus L. was sequenced (224,973 bp, 54.5% A/T), encoding 54 protein-coding genes, 21 tRNAs, and 3 rRNAs, plus SSR/repeat features and 10 chloroplast-derived segments. Synteny with 11 Asteraceae species showed 94.77% identity with Aster batangensis with extensive rearrangement. Most genes showed purifying selection except nad1. Phylogenetically A. indicus is closest to A. batangensis, with Aster close to Erigeron. This enriches Asteraceae genetic resources.

papers.title: Short communication - the advantages of omitting iron hematoxylin in the Masson's trichrome stain.
papers.summary: This short communication reports the advantages of omitting the iron hematoxylin step in the Masson's trichrome collagen stain. The resulting dichromatic stain (red cytoplasm, blue/green collagen, unstained nuclei) abbreviates staining time and reduces cost while preserving overall stain quality, offering a practical modification for routine histology laboratories constrained by workflow, budget, or reagent availability.
